name: audit_an_evict_across_a_holder_reset_is_unjoined
note: the reset is an identity boundary inside ONE producer run (spec 2.3): engine-space ids are comparable only within one engine process, and the reset record is what makes that process boundary visible -- so the pre-reset store is not a join candidate at all, and an evict after the boundary has NO strictly-prior store: unjoined, never a lost promise. A reader keyed only on incarnation gets this wrong in exactly the way the cross-run fixture cannot catch
